problem_statement:
A `BoolWithInverseFlag` in a combined short-option token is set to false

## My urfave/cli version is

v3.13.0, and `main` at 4fa44ab.

## Checklist

- [x] Are you running the latest v3 release? The list of releases is [here](https://github.com/urfave/cli/releases).
- [x] Did you check the manual for your release? The v3 manual is [here](https://cli.urfave.org/v3/getting-started/)
- [x] Did you perform a search about this problem? Here's the [GitHub guide](https://help.github.com/en/github/managing-your-work-on-github/using-search-to-filter-issues-and-pull-requests) about searching.

## Dependency Management

- My project is using go modules.

## Describe the bug

With `UseShortOptionHandling`, a `BoolWithInverseFlag` named inside a combined short-option token comes out false: `-cv` sets `color` to false, while `-c -v` sets it to true.

## To reproduce

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"github.com/urfave/cli/v3"
)

func main() {
	for _, args := range [][]string{{"app", "-c", "-v"}, {"app", "-cv"}, {"app", "-vc"}} {
		cmd := &cli.Command{
			Name:                   "app",
			UseShortOptionHandling: true,
			Flags: []cli.Flag{
				&cli.BoolWithInverseFlag{Name: "color", Aliases: []string{"c"}},
				&cli.BoolFlag{Name: "verbose", Aliases: []string{"v"}},
			},
			Action: func(_ context.Context, cmd *cli.Command) error {
				fmt.Printf("%v: color=%v verbose=%v\n", args[1:], cmd.Bool("color"), cmd.Bool("verbose"))
				return nil
			},
		}
		if err := cmd.Run(context.Background(), args); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		}
	}
}
```

## Observed behavior

```
[-c -v]: color=true verbose=true
[-cv]: color=false verbose=true
[-vc]: color=false verbose=true
```

No error is returned, and `cmd.IsSet("color")` is true in all three cases. The position of the letter in the token makes no difference; the plain `BoolFlag` in the same token is set correctly.

## Expected behavior

`-cv` and `-vc` to set `color` to true, as `-c -v` does.

## Additional context

Tested on v3.13.0 and on current `main` (4fa44ab), with go1.27.1 darwin/arm64.

BTW, this was found by an automated program that writes property-based tests for various open source projects using [hegel](https://github.com/hegeldev/hegel-go) (but it has been reviewed by hand before reporting). We've also potentially found (but not yet hand validated) 7 other bugs in cli. You can see the tests at https://github.com/hegeldev/hegel-zoo/tree/main/targets/go/cli. Let us know if you would like us to file the other bugs found and/or contribute the tests. NB the tests are currently LLM generated and probably not yet suitable for inclusion as is, but we're happy to help get them into a better state if you want them.
